title: fix(sse): correct chunk framing and partial-JSON replay for OpenAI compat streaming
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: customers observed malformed events and premature JSON parse errors when using the OpenAI-compat SSE shim in long-running streams (notably with tool/function-calling payloads). Symptoms included 'Unexpected end of JSON input' in the SDK adapter, spurious empty events due to trailing delimiters, and out-of-order token vs event propagation when partial objects were emitted across chunk boundaries. Repro: run a streaming function call that emits a large 'arguments' payload, interrupt network (simulate cell network) and resume; parsing fails reproducibly. Root cause: the compat layer relied on naive delimiter splitting (newline/data: heuristics) and attempted JSON.parse on individual chunks rather than buffering partial object text while respecting string/escape semantics. This produced parse errors for valid messages that were simply split mid-object. Additionally, the old code treated any empty 'data:' line as a no-op but that interacted badly with CRLF split sequences producing zero-length events. Fix: implement a stateful SSE framing buffer that accumulates incoming bytes until a complete event payload is detected. Event completeness is determined by a robust boundary detector: prefer explicit length-prefix when present; otherwise use JSON-aware bracket counting with string/escape awareness and a small safety timeout to avoid head-of-line blocking. Special-case handlers added for: 1) function/tool call JSON objects that may include nested braces and brackets; 2) 'data: [DONE]' canonical termination; 3) empty-data lines and stray CR/LF sequences. We also added an idempotent partial-replay mechanism: on reconnect, the client can request the last-event-id and the server will include a short replay token that the parser uses to dedupe already processed partial objects. Tests: unit tests cover mid-object chunk splits, CRLF edge cases, multi-event batches in a single TCP segment, and a simulated reconnect/replay flow. Performance: microbenchmarks show negligible (~1%) overhead for the buffering logic on typical 8k payloads; long-tail benefits due to reduced error retry. Migration notes: SDKs using the old shim should not need changes; the behavioral fix is backwards-compatible but fixes previously-observed parse failures. Checklist: - [x] Add robust SSE framing and buffered parser - [x] Add tests for partial JSON and delimiter edge cases - [x] Fix function-calling event ordering and replay dedupe - [x] Add TypeScript shim parity for browser client - [x] Update README/changelog entry - [x] Run perf microbench and e2e streaming smoke tests Release notes: Fixes streaming parse failures and delimiter bugs in the OpenAI-compat SSE shim; improves stability for function/tool-calling streams and reconnect replay. Related: Linear ENG-4821 (streaming regressions), ENG-4875 (compat shim reliability), SUP-1349 (customer incident) End of description.
